title: Cobalt Instrument Studio
subtitle: Engineering Report on Simulation and Verification

blocks.text: Cobalt Instrument Studio is an original static React and TypeScript simulator. One seeded model drives accepted readings, trends, and diagnostics. Versioned telemetry validation protects six instruments across five guided scenarios. Version 0.2.0 adds Gauges, Engine, Trends, Faults, and ACK device pages with a graphite bezel, metallic rings, cobalt blue accents, and large white readouts.

The earlier core revision was merged through PR 1 at main 453ea4, with 92 unit and 12 Linux Chromium browser tests and verified production sites. The current local version 0.2.0 functionality and privacy correction have separate evidence. Publication through reviewed PRs, main CI, updated hosting, and a new annotated tag is approved after final validation. The initial v0.1.0 Release is preserved.

blocks.text: Simulation scope

SIMULATED - NOT LIVE EQUIPMENT. Every value is generated locally. There is no backend, authentication, equipment connection, hardware control, certification, or production guarantee. Demonstration relationships and plausibility ranges are not calibrated equipment measurements or safe operating limits.

One typed reducer owns the simulation session. Commands advance a fixed-step seeded engine; simulated transport then supplies an unknown sample envelope to validation. Only accepted canonical telemetry reaches shared readings, metric rules, history, gauges, and the device preview. Rejected deliveries leave that accepted state intact while time and freshness age continue advancing.

blocks.text: Pure modules under src/engine define model, validation, rules, and display layout. Browser LocalStorage holds validated application preferences; telemetry, events, and device layout stay in session memory. Operation requires no server API, device runtime, or remote data source.

The flat version 1 envelope requires contractVersion, time, rpm, oilPressure, coolantTemp, batteryVoltage, fuelLevel, and engineLoad as own properties. Version must be numeric 1. Channel/time values must be finite numbers; no string coercion is performed. Additional fields are ignored and are never copied into accepted telemetry.

rows: At least 0; no future time; strictly newer than last accepted sample

blocks.text: Rejected delivery and freshness

Malformed envelopes, unsupported versions, missing fields, wrong types, nonfinite/out-of-bounds values, negative/future time, duplicate timestamps, and out-of-order timestamps each produce an explicit rejection reason. A rejected attempt does not replace readings, update accepted time, append history, or count toward metric debounce. Age is measured from the last accepted timestamp.

Each rejection code is logged once per continuous rejection episode; repeats increase a counter without repeated messages. An accepted delivery records one recovery and resets the episode. A sustained invalid episode can therefore produce both sample-quality evidence and the normal communication timeout. Events remain capped at 100.
Distinct bounds and clocks

These are demonstration plausibility limits, broader than the generator and display ranges. A narrowed preview scale preserves the numeric reading and clamps its needle. The 500 ms timer is a scheduling target, not a real-time guarantee. Pause freezes simulation time and age; reset/replay establishes a fresh ordering baseline. See docs/TELEMETRY_CONTRACT.md for the complete acceptance policy.
Normal operating ramp

Expected: increase idle speed and load smoothly while pressure follows and temperature responds slowly. Observed seed 27041 at 35 simulated seconds: {{normalRPM}} rpm, {{normalLoad}} percent load, {{normalOil}} psi oil pressure, and {{normalCoolant}} degrees F coolant. Default rules remained normal. Replay resets accepted data, ordering, history, and diagnostics while retaining valid application preferences.
Coolant overheat

Expected: cooling degradation starts at 6 s and crosses warning and critical. The retained seed/default policy reaches warning at 14.0 s (223.5 degrees F) and critical at 18.5 s (236.8 degrees F). Thresholds are 220/235 degrees F, with 4 degrees F hysteresis and two accepted samples of debounce. Escalation renews acknowledgment; reset creates a normal session.
Oil pressure loss and recovery

Expected: lower generated pressure from 5 s, cross 24 psi warning and 16 psi critical, then restore generation at 24 s. Observed warning was 11.5 s/22.199 psi; critical 15.5 s/14.726 psi; recovery through warning 26.0 s/23.410 psi; normal 27.5 s/30.110 psi. The 3 psi recovery margin and two accepted samples govern clearing. Its 42 s replay accepted 85 samples with no rejection; browser checks exercise acknowledgment and renewed acknowledgment after escalation.

blocks.text: All times describe the simulator. Thermal and pressure fault kinetics are accelerated explanatory assumptions, not real machinery response or field calibration.

rows: No delivery from 5 s through 16.5 s. Retain the 4.5 s sample; default timeout begins at 6.5 s. Valid delivery resumes at 17 s.
Reject nonfinite, missing/wrong-type, duplicate, and out-of-order attempts from 5 s through 16.5 s. Retain accepted values/history; timeout and recovery follow accepted time.

blocks.text: Both scenarios distinguish the internal generated model from accepted readings. A missing or rejected sample cannot hide age by replacing receivedAt. The trend leaves a gap over missing accepted measurements. A valid sample at 17 s restores freshness and communication normal state; invalid-delivery recovery also closes the rejection episode.

blocks.text: Expected versus observed evidence

Observed invalid replay: 24 rejected attempts; first reason events at 5, 8, 9.5, 11, and 14 s; retained 4.5 s readings; timeout at 6.5 s; one delivery recovery and communication clear at 17 s. At 25 s, accepted count/history were 27. Unit/browser checks verify isolation, age, counts, acknowledgment, and recovery. Guided browser clocks do not establish real network or hardware reliability.

The workspace combines five device pages, a six-signal browser, and a selected-slot property editor. A graphite bezel, metallic gauge rings, cobalt blue accents, and large white readouts make the preview resemble an instrument panel. Accepted readings, bounded history, and central diagnostics supply every page. Display bindings, labels, and ranges affect presentation without changing engine commands or alarm thresholds.

The hardening revision makes invalid data, reproducible faults, and display configuration reviewable before equipment integration. A real deployment needs separate connectivity, safety, security, calibration, and operational evidence.

blocks.text: Deliberate tradeoffs

A static frontend avoids server, credential, and equipment dependencies. A central reducer exposes replay/state ownership. Strict acceptance preserves trustworthy displayed data at the cost of stale readings when delivery is invalid. Fixed steps favor repeatability over real-time fidelity. Session-only buffers and display layout keep retention explicit; their caps do not prove a total heap bound.

The application cannot command a physical machine, prove a sensor fault, certify an alarm policy, or replace operational monitoring. The Design concept label identifies an independent engineering demonstration.
Published core and local follow up

PR 1 published telemetry validation, five guided scenarios, device configuration, accessibility changes, and inspectable CI. Version 0.2.0 adds five device pages with blue cockpit styling and corrected test-evidence handling. The central engine, accepted-sample boundary, three application views, simulation disclaimer, display-only properties, preferences, and two static hosting bases are preserved.
Prioritized future engineering
P0: real gateway adapter; calibrated device schema/identity; hardware in the loop; connectivity security/isolation; Safari/Firefox and physical mobile coverage; formal accessibility audit.

P1: jitter/intermittent/simultaneous faults; durable history; validated alarm routing; accountable configuration audit; independent device streams; versioned layout import/export; authorized physical configuration transactions.

P2: additional widgets/layout editing; target display runtime/export; long-session performance profiling; release provenance/rollback; production observability; calibrated simulation models. The roadmap records benefit and complexity for 19 specific future items and separately marks implemented work.
Publication boundary

Version 0.2.0 publication is approved after final QA and passing CI. The earlier main 453ea4 passed PR/main CI and both providers were verified. Main protection requires PRs, strict CI from GitHub Actions, administrator enforcement and resolved conversations; reviewer approvals are zero. Two affected temporary test artifacts were removed after approval. New UI/privacy publication and release results are recorded only after actual execution.

The annotated v0.1.0 tag and its initial two report assets are unchanged. Version 0.2.0 aligns package, changelog, notes, and report metadata. The tag workflow verifies that agreement and reruns CI before publishing one Release with engineering PDF/DOCX, a tested static archive, manifest, and SHA-256 checksums. Its actual new-version execution and downloads remain to be verified.
